A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Outlier Gradient Analysis work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic-data experiments, vision and NLP evaluations, LLM prompt-identification results, and appendix ablations and distribution-shift experiments.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and adds GEX/TRAK benchmark results and reported memory failures in Appendix C.8.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same gradient extraction, outlier detection, and trimming procedure. The iForest/L1/L2 variants, sparse random projection, class-specific LLM estimators, and OneClassSVM distribution-adaptation procedure are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic datasets, CIFAR noise scenarios, ImageNet subset, four GLUE tasks, three LLM benchmarks, and ACS-Income distribution shifts. The added comparator experiments use existing CIFAR coverage.

E2.justification: v5 Appendix C.8 and Table 12 add evaluated GEX and TRAK comparators for CIFAR-10N Aggregate, Random, and Worst settings. Neither has reported comparison scores in v3; existing comparator sets elsewhere are retained.

E3.justification: Reported splits, noise rates, trimming budgets, model configurations, metrics, and training schedules remain unchanged. GEX/TRAK are described as using the existing experimental setup. The test-set adaptation exception clarified in v5 Appendix B.2.5 was already documented in v3 Appendix C.8.

E4.justification: The trimming-budget and tree-count ablations, runtime analyses, qualitative examples, and distribution-shift tests are retained. v3 Appendix C.8 becomes v5 C.9. The new comparator benchmark does not introduce a distinct ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Five-run CIFAR accuracy/standard-deviation reporting, three-run NLP reporting, and LLM uncertainty summaries remain unchanged. The new comparator table introduces no new repeated-run disclosure, uncertainty estimator, or significance test.

E6.justification: v5 Table 12 adds GEX scores of 90.67/89.13/80.30 and TRAK scores of 91.73/90.07/83.52 for Aggregate/Random/Worst. Existing outlier-gradient scores are repeated: L1 exceeds both comparators throughout, while TRAK exceeds iForest on Aggregate and L2 on Worst. Appendix C.8 also reports CIFAR-100N out-of-memory failures for both comparators. Retained tables and figure results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2), Observation 3.1, Hypothesis 3.2, and the computational-complexity expressions in Table 7 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: connecting detrimental-sample identification to gradient outliers, avoiding Hessian inversion, and demonstrating efficient performance across vision and language applications. Conclusion rewriting does not change their scope.

C2.justification: Compared with v3 Appendix D, v5 Section 10 adds explicit limitations concerning high-quality data without gradient outliers and the difficulty of choosing the outlier budget. It removes the diffusion-model future-work suggestion. Appendix C.8 additionally interprets GEX/TRAK memory failures as computational shortcomings.

D1.justification: The code-access reference changes from an anonymous repository in v3 Appendix E to an author-identified GitHub repository in v5 Appendix D. Hardware and implementation settings remain unchanged. The last-checkpoint restriction for Gradient Tracing is relocated from a footnote to Appendix B.2.5.

R1.justification: v5 adds citations to Park et al. (2023) on TRAK, Askari et al. (2025), and Touvron et al. (2023). GEX was already cited through Kim et al. (2024), but is now empirically contrasted. The established related-work narrative is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v5 makes limited wording and grammar edits, rewrites the conclusion, moves and expands the limitations section into the main text, relocates a baseline footnote, and adds acknowledgments. Most explanatory prose and the section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and bibliography undergo a document-wide conversion from single-column presentation to the ICML two-column layout, with substantial changes to table and algorithm sizing and placement. Table 12 is added and the former Table 12 becomes Table 13. All four underlying figure images are retained, with some caption edits.

improvement.justification: The added GEX/TRAK comparison fills a limited empirical comparison gap, while Section 10 states useful applicability and budget-selection limitations absent from v3. These improve empirical context and transparency. The gain is modest: the new comparison lacks baseline-specific implementation and uncertainty details and does not establish superiority for every outlier-gradient variant in every setting.
